pr_title: Add support for last comment edit
pr_body:
Fixes #3613 

Add `--edit-last` option to `issue/pr comment`.
This option edits the last comment that you are the author of. If the comment does not exist, a new one is added.
This is mainly useful when editing comments by the bot.
pr_comments:
Now works in combination with other commands.
`--editor --edit-last`: The last comment can be edited in the editor
`--web --edit-last`: The last comment can be displayed on the web

As a person who first floated the idea of "upsert" functionality in the original issue, I don't think that this functionality needs or should be part of `--edit-last`, since that would be a misnomer. I think `--edit-last` should only edit the last comment and error out if there isn't an existing one.

I went ahead and made the change to remove the upsert functionality and also I fixed the issue with comparing username strings for bots by switching to use the `ViewerDidAuthor` field on comments. By not relying on there username string I was also able to remove the API call to retrieve the current user.

issue_context.title: Support updating comments/reviews
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

As part of CI, I'd like to drop a comment with the metrics of the PR.
For example like codecov does with coverage report.

As the PR is updated, I'd like to delete my initial comment and create a new one, or update my original comment.

### Proposed solution

`comment` commands should support accepting a comment reference for example `--update issuecomment-123123123` and update the comment instead of creating a new one.

`--json comments` should include comment IDs to be able to query them via jq.
comments: This would be a really, reeeeally helpful enhancement, and obviate the need for a lot of custom actions / scripts that are currently needed to upsert comments on a PR. 🙏🏽
Should be possible to delete comments as well.

We've discussed this and decided that due to UI concerns, we wouldn't add a command to edit a comment by ID, since the user would be burdened with having to discover that ID in the first place, but we are open to a contribution that adds a command or flag that edits one's own last comment in a thread.

For example:
```sh
gh issue comment 123 --edit-last
#=> edit my own last comment in issue thread #123
```

How does this sound?
That would cover my use case, at least (a bot that comments helm chart diffs)

@pete-woods @mnquintana Thanks for chiming in. Does the bot ever need to perform an upsert, meaning "use this text to create a new comment or update an existing one"? Do you feel that should be exposed as part of this functionality as well?
I thought that was the same as the previous thing you said. The bot wants to update its single comment with the latest version of the diff.

To clarify, the first thing I said was a feature that only edits an existing comment by the same actor. If the comment to edit does not exist, the operation would fail.

An "upsert" is a single operation that would (in the context of comments) edit an existing comment, and create a comment if one by the same actor doesn't exist. I thought that the upsert operation might be useful for bots.

Okay, got it. So what I need is definitely to be able to "upsert" somehow. Though I don't mind if it's multiple commands (like finding if I've already commented and then using an update comment command), as long as I don't have to start using curl.

> We've discussed this and decided that due to UI concerns, we wouldn't add a command to edit a comment by ID, since the user would be burdened with having to discover that ID in the first place, but we are open to a contribution that adds a command or flag that edits one's own last comment in a thread.

Personally, I don't think needing to first find a comment's ID and then updating via that ID should be a blocker to supporting the ability to update comments directly. I mostly use gh CLI for scripting and often need to first find the PR or issue number before I can run commands against that issue, so I don't see why I wouldn't be able to do the same thing for comments.

I would be fine with an `--edit-last` flag  as it would solve my immediate use case. But I think gh CLI would be incomplete without a way to edit comments directly. Especially since you can already do it via the rest API (although its a lot more code)

> > We've discussed this and decided that due to UI concerns, we wouldn't add a command to edit a comment by ID, since the user would be burdened with having to discover that ID in the first place, but we are open to a contribution that adds a command or flag that edits one's own last comment in a thread.
> 
> Personally, I don't think needing to first find a comment's ID and then updating via that ID should be a blocker to supporting the ability to update comments directly. I mostly use gh CLI for scripting and often need to first find the PR or issue number before I can run commands against that issue, so I don't see why I wouldn't be able to do the same thing for comments.
> 
> I would be fine with an `--edit-last` flag as it would solve my immediate use case. But I think gh CLI would be incomplete without a way to edit comments directly. Especially since you can already do it via the rest API (although its a lot more code)

I think `--edit-last` is a great solution for a lot of use cases, and I also agree with @Pearce-Ropion that it may not cover all use cases.

I may have a CI workflow that needs to post and then later update different comments on the PR.  It might post one comment to link to build artifacts, and append this as the build progresses.  Another comment might be updated to show test results as they progress.

It's true there's no standard approach to search for the comment to update, In my case I just index comments using a tag hidden inside an HTML comment at the start of the comment: `<!--tag-->`

I can then find the comment to update with something like:

```
gh api \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28" \
  /repos/OWNER/REPO/issues/PULL_NUMBER/comments  --jq 'map(select(.body|startswith("<!--tag-->"))) | .[0].id'  
  ```

Would it be possible to add the removal/deletion behavior that works similar to `--edit-last`?
e.g. `gh pr comment --edit-last --delete` or `gh pr comment --remove-last`


That way, deleting would be possible without the burden of associating a comment to an ID value.
Created a new issue for this so we can keep this thread dead - https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/10366
